summary: New sense 1: sich stemmen; sich verfangen (Detrans.)
rationale: Supplies a gloss for the single implicit Detransitive group already represented by bull-against-bull Preterit and k-midaqər Infectum. Human reciprocal bracing is a participant extension of that group.

data.turoyo: huwe w Sifuk mdaqri qum ḥḏoḏe bar rumaḥ.
data.translation: Da standen sich Abu Sêd und Ssifûk mit den Lanzen gegenüber;

rationale: Thin Detransitive Preterit cell, one inherited grammar example; first contextual textual example with plural human subjects, reciprocal qum and overt lances.

summary: The one supplied occurrence is securely confrontational and reciprocal. The inherited II Detransitive mdaqər and plural mdaqri provide a reasonable formal comparison; no L-series agent suffix is present.
The selected excerpt is a whole simple clause, retaining the edition’s German names and punctuation. The following threat is unnecessary for identifying the posture and is cut.
qum ḥḏoḏe codes facing each other, and bar rumaḥ supplies lances. No ordinary Detransitive agent phrase or transitive object is introduced.

The clause presents a confrontation posture; the supplied text does not settle whether mdaqri introduces entry into that state or describes its result. Its glossary Preterit placement is retained provisionally rather than creating a new Part. Pass. box.
Does mdaqri at PrS 6/40 denote taking up a braced stance or an already established posture? Confirm the event/result interpretation within the inherited Detransitive Preterit filing.
How closely is the human qum ḥḏoḏe construction related to bull entanglement and to literal sich stemmen? Further contexts could establish a finer division, but this one does not require it.

rationale: The static location introduced by in den requires the dative plural Hörnern. The current Hörner omits its final -n.

summary: Two human opponents stand/braced facing each other with lances, compared with the inherited bull-against-bull example. qum ḥḏoḏe makes the reciprocal orientation explicit; human participants do not by themselves create a new sense.
